paragraphs: Rabbi Chananyah, son of Rabbi Yehoshua.
Mentioned in Bamidbar Rabbah 10:4. Hyman calls this a scribal error and proposes R’ Chananyah [ר״ח], the son of Rabbi Yehoshua’s brother, as in Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:6.

notes.text: The precise Midrash Rabbah book is not established here. The abbreviation ר״ח is retained without choosing between Chananyah and Chanina; the proposed relation is nephew, not son.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Sanhedrin chapter-2 scalar in halakhah index5 names Chananyah, son of Rabbi Yehoshua’s brother. This supports Chananyah in the cited parallel and nephew rather than son. It does not identify the Midrash Rabbah book abbreviated מ״ר or prove the alleged error there. Hyman owns the proposed correction; no new full-chapter absence claim is made.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. II, p. 507) cites Midrash Rabbah as פ״י־ד. The supplied Hebrew transcription has פי״ד, formerly read as chapter 14. The passage is Bamidbar Rabbah 10:4. In the discussion of Solomon, it attributes the interpretation of Deuteronomy 7:3 to Chananyah son of Rabbi Yehoshua. Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:6 gives the same interpretation to Chananyah son of Rabbi Yehoshua’s brother. Hyman calls the former wording a scribal error and proposes the latter as the correction. The two readings are preserved as textual witnesses.
